method: built-in image generation; lighting-weather edit; single generated variant
prompt:
Use case: lighting-weather. Edit target: the provided clean P143 virtual aerial map. Produce ONE photorealistic deepest-night variant for a website crossfade. CRITICAL: keep exactly the same 16:9 frame, camera, horizon, coastline, river, road geometry, trees, every mountain silhouette and ALL building positions and sizes. No zoom, no crop, no reframing, no redesign, no new buildings. Keep the original map coordinate alignment. Change only night illumination and sky appearance.
Night: deep navy, subdued natural moonlit landscape, recognizable mountain and shoreline details, dark ocean. In the existing thin visible sky strip above the far horizon at the upper left/top add sparse small realistic stars, a restrained starry-night feeling. Stars only in sky, never over land or ocean; do not expand sky. Remove daytime orange sunlight.
Bake fixed warm lighting INTO this night raster: (1) lower-right city has a believable distribution of amber and warm-white lit windows, subtle urban street lighting, mostly dark roofs; not every window lit; (2) evenly spaced modest warm streetlamps and small pools of light tracing existing paved roads through the valley and mountains, following their actual curves; small lights far away, slightly larger near foreground, no luminous dashed graphic route; (3) the tiny beach cabin near lower-left x~33% y~71% glows warmly through its windows, the central Japanese pine/bamboo garden complex x~50% y~45% has lit interior windows and veranda, the distant temple x~40% y~23% has quiet warm interior lamps, the snow mountain house x~82% y~17% has warm windows, and city apartment interiors x~82% y~74% feel warmly occupied. Keep their shapes and locations EXACTLY. Warm lights remain restrained and inviting, not neon, not overexposed; do not floodlight the forest. Calm premium photographic realism.
No text, labels, pins, white trails, UI, borders, watermarks, illustration or added moon. Output a single full-bleed night map matching the input aspect and layout.
notes: Fixed raster lighting, no SVG animation. Day and night share the existing 1672×941 CSS map coordinate system; original raster 1671×941, generated raster 1670×941. Major coast, roads and building landmarks visually checked in ~53% night crossfade; not a pixel-identical reconstruction.
